subject: Re: Renewal agreements alignment & capacity bump — MSA/orderform coordination
messages:
From: Joe Lee <joe.lee@taloncloud.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, May 3, 2027 at 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity increase — next steps & redlines

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with renewal discussions — our current term ends 2027-06-30 and we expect traffic to triple over the next 9 months. High-level asks: 

- Increase committed capacity from 100 units to 300 units (see attached current order form)
- Move to a 24-month committed term in exchange for the committed pricing band
- Clarify billing cadence (we prefer consolidated monthly invoicing)

I've attached a short request PDF and our current order form for reference. Can you confirm who on your side will handle legal redlines and whether Redwood can support a 24-month term with a staged capacity ramp (50% Year 1 / 50% Year 2)?

Attachements: Talon_Renewal_Request_20270503.pdf, Current_OrderForm.pdf

Thanks,
Joe Lee
Head of Platform | Talon Cloud
joe.lee@taloncloud.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: Joe Lee <joe.lee@taloncloud.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, May 4, 2027 at 08:45 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase — next steps & redlines

Joe — appreciate the clear asks. Happy to get this moving. Proposed next steps: 

1) I'll loop in Legal to draft redlines to the MSA and a revised order form (cc'd internally).
2) Please confirm the desired capacity schedule (example: 100 -> 200 on 2027-10-01 -> 300 on 2028-04-01).
3) Finance question: billing cadence — you indicated consolidated monthly invoicing; is net-30 acceptable or do you need net-45?
4) Goal: get redlines to you by EOD 5/4 so we can start DocuSign by early next week if we have alignment.

If that timeline works, I will ask Legal to produce a tracked MSA and an order-form draft with the staged ramp and the 24-month term.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Lauren — looping in with a first pass of tracked redlines. See attached: Redwood_MSA_redline_20270504.docx and OrderForm_Talon_v2.xlsx. Key points called out in the redline (summary):

- Term & renewal: proposed 24-month initial term with an auto-renewal thereafter; customer asked for 24 months in exchange for committed pricing. Legal: we are ok with 24 months but propose a 60-day renewal notice (customer later requests 90 — see below).
- Capacity ramp: added a capacity schedule appendix to the order form with staged dates (you asked for staged ramp — see schedule tab).
- Data handling / retention: tightened language around retention, logging, and audit evidence to match Private deployment options (we flagged a couple of optional KMS provisions).
- Liability/indemnity: adjusted cap language consistent with Redwood precedence; noted this will be a negotiation point if Talon requests higher limitation exceptions.
- Billing: default net-30; if Talon requires net-45 we'll need Finance sign-off (cc Marcus).

Please forward to Talon and advise on which points we should be more flexible on.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redline_20270504.docx (redline), OrderForm_Talon_v2.xlsx (capacity schedule)

Diego / Lauren — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. Our legal team reviewed and we can accept the majority of the changes. A few items to call out: 

- Renewal notice: we need the renewal notice window extended to 90 days (we generally operate on 90-day cancellation notice for 24-month deals).
- Billing cadence: Talon requires net-45 (we run a consolidated pay cycle at EOM + 45).
- Capacity schedule: the staged ramp in the OrderForm looks good; can you add an acceptance milestone after the 2nd stage (quick operational sign-off)?

I've attached our annotated redlines for your reference (Talon_legal_redlines.pdf). If you can accept the 90-day notice and net-45, we're ready to move to DocuSign.

Best,
Maya Singh

Team — quick summary and owners so we can close this week: 

Summary of negotiated points (customer confirmed in-line acceptance):
- Term: 24-month initial term — agreed.
- Renewal notice: customer requested 90 days; Legal has flagged 60 as standard. Diego: please confirm acceptability of 90 in this deal (I think we can concede given the revenue profile).
- Capacity: staged ramp (100 -> 200 -> 300) documented in OrderForm_Talon_v2.xlsx; customer requested an operational acceptance milestone after stage 2 — add as a short acceptance clause.
- Billing: Talon requires net-45. Marcus: please confirm finance is OK; if not, we need a short rationale to share with the customer.
- DocuSign: once legal confirms renewal notice we will assemble the envelope and send to Talon.

Action items: 
- Diego Fernandez: confirm whether Redwood accepts 90-day renewal notice for RW-4592 by EOD 5/9.
- Marcus Lin: confirm net-45 billing acceptability or provide alternative by 5/10.
- Marissa Cole: prepare capacity ramp credit schedule and run final pricing math to include in the order form.
- Lauren: I will prepare the DocuSign envelope pending Diego/Marcus sign-off and target signature by 5/12. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4592 (RW-4592). DocuSign placeholder: https://www.docusign.com/en/sign?envelopeId=abc123-placeholder
